blocks.passage:
Good negotiation is not about winning against the other side. It is about building an agreement that both sides actually want to honour after the handshake. The difference is enormous, both in outcome and in the relationship afterwards.

Skilled negotiators rarely give anything for free. They trade: "If you can commit to a larger volume, we could look at a better price". Each concession is linked to something they receive in return. That keeps the process fair and visible to everyone.

Equally important is understanding what the other side actually wants — not what they say first. Their opening position is usually less important than the interests behind it. Ask questions, listen for clues, and be patient. The best deals come from understanding, not from pressure.

items.q: According to the text, good negotiation is about…
options: building an agreement both sides want to honour
items.why: "building an agreement that both sides actually want to honour after the handshake."

items.q: What do skilled negotiators do instead of giving things for free?
options: They trade — each concession is linked to something in return
items.why: "They trade… Each concession is linked to something they receive in return."

items.q: Why is trading described as keeping the process "fair and visible"?
options: Because each side can see what is being exchanged
items.why: Inferência: quando cada concessão está ligada a uma contrapartida, o que se troca fica à vista de todos.

items.q: What does the text say is usually less important than it seems?
items.why: "Their opening position is usually less important than the interests behind it."

items.q: Where, according to the text, do the best deals come from?
items.why: "The best deals come from understanding, not from pressure."

audio.text:
Thanks for coming in. Before we talk numbers, I want to understand what matters most to you this year — is it price, or is it certainty of supply?

Right, so certainty is the priority. That's useful, because it tells me where we can create value for both of us.

Here's my thinking. If you can commit to a twelve-month contract rather than rolling monthly, we could look at locking the price for the whole year. You get certainty; we get a stable volume to plan around.

And if you can bring the volume up to the higher tier, we could shorten the lead time as well. I'm not giving that away for nothing — it only works if the volume is there.

What I'd rather avoid is haggling line by line. Tell me the two or three things you really need, and I'll tell you honestly what we can and can't do. If we're both acting in good faith, we'll get to a deal that holds.

items.q: What does Oliver want to understand before talking numbers?
options: What matters most to the other side — price or certainty
items.why: "I want to understand what matters most to you this year — is it price, or is it certainty of supply?"

items.q: What does Oliver offer in return for a twelve-month contract?
options: Locking the price for the whole year
items.why: "If you can commit to a twelve-month contract… we could look at locking the price for the whole year."

items.q: What condition does Oliver attach to shortening the lead time?
options: Bringing the volume up to the higher tier
items.why: "if you can bring the volume up to the higher tier, we could shorten the lead time… it only works if the volume is there."

items.q: What does Oliver want to avoid?
items.why: "What I'd rather avoid is haggling line by line."

items.q: What does Oliver believe will produce a deal that holds?
options: Both sides acting in good faith
items.why: "If we're both acting in good faith, we'll get to a deal that holds."

items.q: "We made one **concession** and got two in return." A concession is…
options: something you give up to reach a deal
items.why: Concession = concessão, algo que você cede.

items.q: A **win-win** outcome is one where…
items.why: Win-win = ganha-ganha, os dois lados ganham.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Their opening ___ was high, but their real interest was fast delivery."
items.why: Position = posição (declarada); interest é o interesse por trás dela.

items.q: The **lead time** is…
options: the time between order and delivery
items.why: Lead time = prazo entre pedido e entrega.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "That's my ___ — below it, there's no deal."
items.why: Walk-away point = ponto de retirada, o limite abaixo do qual não há acordo.

items.q: "Let's **meet in the middle** on the price." To meet in the middle means to…
items.why: Meet in the middle = chegar a um meio-termo.

items.q: "I can't move on price, but I can **throw in** free delivery." To throw in means to…
items.why: Throw in = incluir sem custo adicional.

items.q: "If the terms don't improve, we may have to **walk away**." To walk away means to…
options: leave the negotiation without a deal
items.why: Walk away = abandonar a negociação sem fechar.

items.q: "Let's **nail down** the volume before we discuss price." To nail down means to…
items.why: Nail down = definir com firmeza.

items.q: "We're close — let's not **haggle over** the last one percent." To haggle over means to…
options: argue about small details of price
items.why: Haggle over = pechinchar/discutir pequenos detalhes de preço.
